scope: Descriptive review of all 45 instruction9_v1 OSC decoding outputs; not a calibrated quality benchmark
method: Single non-blinded assistant review. All 36 new sampling outputs were read in full, with only consecutive identical lines collapsed with counts. Raw text remains unchanged in the source report. The nine greedy generations exactly match the earlier full-ID records; their instruction-following and completion labels and notes are reused from the prior review. Greedy factuality labels are limited assessments of those notes, not a new independent factual audit.

rubric.instruction_following: met/partial/not_met/unclear; includes supplied constraints, requested task and ending
rubric.task_completion: complete/incomplete/unclear; a structural core endpoint, independent of EOS, subsequent tails and correctness. A definite but wrong recommendation can be complete; a process omitting the requested starting or ending stage is incomplete.
rubric.factuality: no_obvious_error/has_error/unclear/not_applicable; supplied-number contradictions and invented material constraints count as errors. Fiction uses not_applicable; coherence defects are recorded in notes. Unclear is not a factuality pass.
rubric.limitations: No external factual audit, blinded reviewers, inter-rater agreement, calibrated acceptance threshold or statistical generalization. EOS and low repeat8 do not imply completion, correctness or usability. Repetition flags are descriptive and may miss semantic repetition or boilerplate. Nucleus changes temperature and top_p jointly. Only two seeds and nine prompts were evaluated.

conclusion: Full-distribution sampling reduced measured repetition and increased EOS in this fixed sample, but seven of eighteen runs still capped and content failures remained. No practical-quality acceptance is established by these results.
